Remaining limitations: several reception witnesses were read from unregistered public deliveries (Augustine on Pss 75 and 118 and De moribus; Cassiodorus on Pss 32, 75, 118; Basil De Spiritu Sancto 16.38; Aquinas Super Mt; Swete's Greek Daniel; Wilson p. 175) and are cited, not bound; Rupert, Durandus, Schuster, Irenaeus, Aquinas Super Eph, Trent and Gueranger were read in optical layers only; no Greek psalm or Daniel commentary, Hilary, Ambrose on Ps 118, Origen or critical sacramentary/Sextuplex edition was reached; the Communion's 'omnes' and the Offertory's Latin source remain unidentified; the chronology corpus carries no traditional psalm attributions, no date for the Gospel's narrated event, and only a duration for the Offertory's setting; the shared translation overlay still marks this Sunday's orations' English unavailable although the Cummiskey passage exists (reported, not changed). Observation for the driver: the medieval commentators and Gueranger show this Sunday's Gospel was Luke 14 or Mt 22:23-33 in older arrangements and Wilson's Gregorian pairs these orations with other chants, so every whole-formulary reading is editorial synthesis; interpretations.md marks this throughout.
summary: Completed the research boundary for the Claude 1962 Dominica XVII post Pentecosten: collated all ten elements (nos. 1602-1611) on the hash-matched CMAA facsimile's native 500 ppi images against the Benziger 1962 and the tracked 1862 Pustet leaves, ran a passage-by-passage reception sweep (Augustine, Chrysostom, Jerome, Gregory, Irenaeus, Basil, Cassiodorus, Aquinas, with Rupert, Durandus, Gueranger, Schuster, Wilson's Gregorian and the Sextuplex for formulary history), generated the canonical chronology record and annotations, and proposed three source-grounded interpretations.
